## Transitioning Your Communications from Tyntec: How to Keep Customer Messages Flowing Seamlessly with Twilio


When facing a platform migration, the goal is simple: your end users shouldn't notice a thing. If you are currently navigating a transition following Tyntec’s recent updates, your priority should be to ensure that behind every API call, a customer can still log into their account, confirm a purchase, or reach a support agent without interruption.


The primary aim is continuity: keeping one-time passwords (OTPs) arriving instantly and customer messages flowing without a single gap in service. If you are evaluating your next steps, Twilio offers a secure and resilient landing point to maintain your current operations, along with an opportunity to build for the future.


Here is how Twilio can help ensure a smooth transition and support your customer engagement going forward.


## Upgrade your verification, don’t just move it


Migrating your user authentication can be more than a simple lift-and-shift; it’s an opportunity to modernize. Verification today is much more than sending an SMS code.


With Twilio, you can[automatically upgrade to](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/messaging/channels/rcs)[RCS](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/messaging/channels/rcs) when it performs better for the end user. If you use[WhatsApp for OTPs](https://www.twilio.com/docs/content/whatsappauthentication) , you aren't charged for undelivered messages. Furthermore, you can reduce friction entirely by utilizing[Silent Network Auth](https://www.twilio.com/docs/verify/sna) and[Passkeys](https://www.twilio.com/docs/verify/passkeys) , which verify users seamlessly without requiring them to type a code at all. Finally, Twilio’s built-in[Fraud Guard](https://www.twilio.com/docs/verify/preventing-toll-fraud/sms-fraud-guard) automatically detects and blocks SMS pumping, protecting your budget from artificial traffic inflation.


## Keep your WhatsApp standing


A major concern during any migration is losing the hard-earned reputation and scale of your existing WhatsApp Business account. Fortunately, Meta offers a direct migration path to Twilio that preserves your core assets.


When you port your number, you keep your display name, messaging-limit tier, quality rating, and Official Business Account (OBA) status. High-quality message templates are also duplicated directly to your new Twilio environment.


Meta does re-review these templates and may reject some, but the underlying reputation and tier of your account remain intact.


This provides concrete reassurance that your WhatsApp operations won't have to start from scratch.


## Maintaining Europe-first credibility and data privacy


Many companies chose Tyntec for its strong European presence and commitment to data privacy. Moving to a new global provider shouldn't mean compromising on those standards.


[Twilio’s IE1 (Ireland) region](https://www.twilio.com/docs/global-infrastructure/messaging-eu-feature-availability) supports strict EU data residency for your SMS traffic. Backed by full GDPR compliance and ISO 27001 certifications, you can confidently migrate knowing your customer data remains secure, localized, and fully aligned with European regulatory requirements.


Data residency is only half of compliance. Before you switch, export your opt-in records, opt-out lists and consent timestamps. A customer who unsubscribed last year should never hear from you again just because you changed providers.


## Scale and resilience you can rely on


For mission-critical communications, scale isn't about boasting: it’s about reassurance. You need a platform that provides peace of mind when it matters most.


Twilio is built on proactive routing and multi-layered redundancy, connecting to over 4,800 carrier networks across 180+ countries. Trusted by more than 335,000 customers, the platform reliably processes 262B+ messages a year. This massive infrastructure ensures that if a localized carrier issue occurs, Twilio automatically optimizes the route to keep your messages moving.


## Room to grow


Migrations require time and resources, so it makes sense to choose a platform you won't outgrow. You can start by simply porting your SMS and OTP workloads to ensure immediate continuity, and then seamlessly add new channels over time.


Operating on a single unified platform allows you to easily expand into RCS, WhatsApp, Voice, and Email (via Twilio SendGrid). If your teams relied on tools like Tyntec’s Inbox,[Twilio Flex](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/flex) provides a highly customizable, omnichannel workspace for your support agents, while Twilio Segment can unify your customer data to drive highly personalized interactions.


Plan for short training sessions, recreate saved replies and templates ahead of go-live and decide early which conversation history needs to move with you. Agents who feel confident on day one keep conversations warm.


## What this looks like in practice


A global luxury fashion retailer relied on Tyntec to power clienteling conversations between store associates and their customers over SMS and WhatsApp, across hundreds of stores worldwide.


[Working with Twilio partner Zennify](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/partners/integrators#/2313928) , the retailer migrated in two phases. First, Zennify moved all their written-channel traffic onto an interim Twilio Flex setup in less than two weeks, so store teams kept talking to their clients with only a minimal gap in service. With continuity secured, the team then built a full native integration on the Twilio Conversations API. That integration gives the retailer a scalable foundation for its clienteling program for years to come.


## A practical, low-risk migration checklist


Migrations are most successful when executed in phases rather than a single flip of a switch. To ensure a zero-downtime transition, follow this low-risk checklist:


1.


**List and prioritize workloads:** Start by identifying your most critical traffic. Always migrate your OTPs and transactional alerts first, as these are the most time-sensitive for your users.


2.


**Export your assets:** Before your current service wraps up, export your sender IDs, approved message templates, and historical delivery data.


3.


**Start sender registrations early:** Some countries require alphanumeric sender IDs to be pre-registered and US traffic requires A2P 10DLC or toll-free verification. Submit these on day one, because approval times are set by carriers and regulators and can’t be sped up.


4.


**Run in parallel:** Set up Twilio alongside your existing integration.


5.


**Phase your traffic:** Begin routing a small percentage of your traffic (e.g., 5-10%) through Twilio. Monitor delivery rates and slowly dial up the volume in phases until 100% of your communications are safely running on the new platform.
